components.note: 手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'
攵 (a striking hand) — 败 relates to being struck down or defeated.
贝 (bèi) gives a sound close to bài, sharing the same initial.

example.hanzi: 拳王在这场比赛中击败了所有对手。
example.pinyin: quánwáng zài zhè chǎng bǐsài zhōng jī bài le suǒyǒu duìshǒu.
example.english: The boxing champion defeated all his opponents in this match.
example.fact: In 2016, Google DeepMind's AlphaGo defeated Go champion Lee Sedol, the first time a computer beat a top professional under standard tournament conditions. The game of Go has more possible board positions than there are atoms in the observable universe, which is why the win stunned AI researchers who had expected it to take another decade.

components.note: 车 (cart) — relates to 转's meaning 'to turn, change direction,' like a wheel turning.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 转 is pronounced zhuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.

example.hanzi: 她听到脚步声，立刻转身查看。
example.pinyin: tā tīngdào jiǎobù shēng, lìkè zhuǎn shēn chákàn.
example.english: She heard footsteps and immediately turned around to look.
example.fact: Owls can rotate their heads up to 270 degrees without cutting off blood flow to the brain. Extra neck vertebrae and specialized blood vessels that pool and reroute blood make this possible, letting an owl scan its surroundings while keeping its body perfectly still to avoid alerting prey.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 统 relates to threads gathered into one continuous strand, extending to the idea of unifying or governing as one system.
充 (chōng) gives a hint of the sound — 统 is pronounced tǒng, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
氵 (water) — 治 relates to managing or controlling the flow of water, such as flood control.
台 (a platform, structure) — a structure used to direct and control water gave 治 its meaning 'to govern' or 'to manage.'

example.hanzi: 罗马帝国曾经统治了地中海周边的大片土地。
example.pinyin: luómǎ dìguó céngjīng tǒngzhì le dìzhōnghǎi zhōubiān de dàpiàn tǔdì.
example.english: The Roman Empire once ruled a vast area surrounding the Mediterranean.
example.fact: At its territorial peak under Emperor Trajan around 117 AD, the Roman Empire spanned roughly 5 million square kilometers across three continents. It was held together by over 400,000 kilometers of roads, some of which still underlie modern European highways today.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 遭 relates to something you come across or run into on your way.
曹 (cáo) gives a sound distantly related to zāo, having drifted apart over time.
辶 (to walk) — encountering someone often happens while moving or traveling.
禺 (yú) gives a sound close to yù, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 登山队在半山腰遭遇了突如其来的暴风雪。
example.pinyin: dēngshān duì zài bànshānyāo zāoyù le tūrúqílái de bàofēngxuě.
example.english: The climbing team encountered a sudden blizzard halfway up the mountain.
example.fact: Above 8,000 meters, mountaineers enter what is called the 'death zone,' where oxygen levels are only about a third of those at sea level. A sudden storm there can drop temperatures by more than 30 degrees Celsius within hours, which is exactly why an unplanned encounter with bad weather at high altitude is so often fatal.

components.note: 无 is the simplified form of 無, which originally depicted a person dancing while holding tasseled ornaments in each hand, a ritual dancer. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the negative 'not have, without,' a meaning unrelated to its original dance imagery.
纟 (thread) — relates directly to 线's meaning 'line, thread, wire.'
戋 (jiān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from xiàn.
电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'

example.hanzi: 二战期间，无线电在军事通讯中起了关键作用。
example.pinyin: èrzhàn qījiān, wúxiàndiàn zài jūnshì tōngxìn zhōng qǐ le guānjiàn zuòyòng.
example.english: During World War II, radio played a crucial role in military communication.
example.fact: In 1901, Guglielmo Marconi transmitted the Morse code letter 'S' by radio across more than 3,000 kilometers of ocean, from Cornwall to Newfoundland. Many scientists at the time thought this was impossible, since they believed the curvature of the Earth would block the signal.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching to take hold of something.
耳 (ear) — from an ancient battlefield practice of taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill, the origin of 取's meaning 'to take, obtain.'
冫 (a contracted form of 水, water) ties 决 to its early sense of a river breaking through a dike or draining a blockage, an image later extended to 'to decide, resolve.'
夬 (jué) is the phonetic component, an exact match for 决's reading.

于 is an ancient character whose original picture is debated; one theory reads it as a curved digging or plowing implement. By the Zhou dynasty it was already used mainly as a grammatical particle meaning 'at, in, than,' with its original concrete meaning lost to history.

example.hanzi: 疫苗的效果取决于接种者的免疫系统状况。
example.pinyin: yìmiáo de xiàoguǒ qǔjuéyú jiēzhòngzhě de miǎnyì xìtǒng zhuàngkuàng.
example.english: The effectiveness of a vaccine depends on the immune system condition of the recipient.
example.fact: Edward Jenner's 1796 smallpox vaccine, made from material taken from cowpox blisters, laid the foundation of modern immunology. Smallpox went on to become the only human disease ever eradicated worldwide, a milestone the World Health Organization officially declared in 1980.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the sea or river being traveled through
斿 — a banner streaming in the wind, evoking free, drifting movement
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.

example.hanzi: 数千名市民走上街头游行，要求改善环境保护政策。
example.pinyin: shùqiān míng shìmín zǒushàng jiētóu yóuxíng, yāoqiú gǎishàn huánjìng bǎohù zhèngcè.
example.english: Thousands of citizens marched through the streets, demanding improved environmental policies.
example.fact: The 1963 March on Washington drew an estimated 250,000 people and is where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his 'I Have a Dream' speech. Historians widely credit the demonstration with helping build the political momentum that led to the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 胡 originally referred to the flesh under an animal's chin or throat
古 (gǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 胡's reading hú
讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō
Two lines curving apart from each other, originally meaning 'to divide, split' — the shape was later adopted to represent the number 'eight.'
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.

example.hanzi: 别听他的，那些话完全是胡说八道。
example.pinyin: bié tīng tā de, nàxiē huà wánquán shì húshuōbādào.
example.english: Don't listen to him, that's complete nonsense.
example.fact: A 2018 MIT study published in Science analyzed millions of tweets and found that false stories spread about six times faster than true ones. Researchers attributed this to novelty: surprising claims trigger more sharing than accurate but ordinary information.

components.note: 开 (open, here representing a frame or opening) — 形 pictures light passing through a gap.
彡 (streaks or rays of light) — light and pattern coming through an opening gave 形 its meaning 'shape' or 'form.'
弋 (an awl or tool) — one of the craftsman's instruments.
工 (a measuring square) — a tool for making things to a fixed pattern, giving 式 its meaning 'style, form, type.'

example.hanzi: 这份报告的形式很正式，但内容有点空洞。
example.pinyin: zhè fèn bàogào de xíngshì hěn zhèngshì, dàn nèiróng yǒudiǎn kōngdòng.
example.english: This report's format is very formal, but the content is a bit empty.
example.fact: Snowflakes almost always grow with six-fold symmetry because water molecules bond into a hexagonal lattice as ice crystallizes. Yet no two snowflakes have ever been proven identical, since tiny shifts in humidity and temperature during formation shape each one in a slightly different way.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嘴 refers directly to the mouth, or a beak-like spout.
觜 (zī) gives a sound distantly related to zuǐ, having drifted apart over time.
Mouth — lips surround the mouth.
Gives the sound chén, related to chún but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 冬天风大，她的嘴唇都干裂了。
example.pinyin: dōngtiān fēng dà, tā de zuǐchún dōu gānliè le.
example.english: The wind was strong in winter, and her lips became chapped.
example.fact: Human lips have no sweat glands or oil glands, and the skin covering them is far thinner than skin elsewhere on the face. This leaves blood vessels closer to the surface, which is why lips look redder than surrounding skin and dry out so much faster in cold or windy weather.

components.note: 矛 is a simplified picture of a long spear, its point aimed up and to the right.
厂 depicts a slanted overhang, here standing for a protective shield.
目 (eye) — an eye peering out from behind the shield 厂 gives 盾 its meaning 'shield.'

example.hanzi: 他的说法前后矛盾，让人难以相信。
example.pinyin: tā de shuōfǎ qiánhòu máodùn, ràng rén nányǐ xiāngxìn.
example.english: His statements contradicted each other, making it hard to believe him.
example.fact: In 1931, mathematician Kurt Gödel proved his incompleteness theorems, showing that any sufficiently powerful mathematical system contains true statements that can never be proven within that system. It was a landmark discovery about the built-in limits of logical consistency itself.

components.note: 王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — a valuable object one might glimpse or notice.
见 (to see) — catching sight of something links to the meanings 'to appear, present, now.'
豕 (pig/boar) — appears as part of 象's original full-body pictograph of an elephant, reusing a four-legged-animal shape; 象 itself depicts an elephant's trunk and ears above the body.

example.hanzi: 温室效应是一种全球性的气候现象。
example.pinyin: wēnshì xiàoyìng shì yī zhǒng quánqiúxìng de qìhòu xiànxiàng.
example.english: The greenhouse effect is a global climate phenomenon.
example.fact: Venus has an atmosphere that is 96 percent carbon dioxide, which drives a runaway greenhouse effect and raises its surface temperature to about 465 degrees Celsius, hot enough to melt lead. That makes Venus the hottest planet in the solar system, even though Mercury sits closer to the sun.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 结 relates to tying or knotting threads together.
吉 (jí) gives a hint of the sound — 结 is pronounced jié, a connection that has shifted over time.
合 pictures a lid (the upper triangular stroke) fitting closed over a container or mouth (口) below, the image of two halves joining together. This gave 合 its meaning 'to combine, join, close, agree.'

example.hanzi: 这种药物结合了两种不同的治疗方式。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng yàowù jiéhé le liǎng zhǒng bùtóng de zhìliáo fāngshì.
example.english: This medicine combines two different treatment approaches.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin by accident in 1928 when mold contaminated a bacterial culture in his lab. Combined with mass-production techniques developed during World War II, it became the first widely used antibiotic, a pairing credited with saving hundreds of millions of lives since.

components.note: 忄 (heart) ties 怪 to an inner feeling, in this case the sense of being startled or unsettled by something unusual.
This 圣 is not the 'sage' character but an unrelated ancient component historically read guài, serving as the phonetic element and an exact match for 怪's sound.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 邻居都觉得他是个怪人，很少和人说话。
example.pinyin: línjū dōu juéde tā shì gè guàirén, hěn shǎo hé rén shuōhuà.
example.english: The neighbors all think he's an eccentric, and he rarely talks to people.
example.fact: Nikola Tesla was famously eccentric, reportedly counting his steps obsessively and requiring exactly 18 napkins at every dinner. Despite these quirks, his work on alternating current still underlies most of the electrical grid used around the world today.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
亻 (a person), shown twice — one person next to another, similar in shape, the source of 似's meaning 'to resemble, similar, like.'

example.hanzi: 这对姐妹的长相非常相似。
example.pinyin: zhè duì jiěmèi de zhǎngxiàng fēicháng xiāngsì.
example.english: The two sisters look very similar.
example.fact: Chimpanzees share about 98.8 percent of their DNA with humans, making them our closest living relatives. The similarity is close enough that some biologists have proposed reclassifying chimpanzees within the same genus as humans.

components.note: 后 originally pictured a ruler issuing a command from an open mouth, and meant 'sovereign, queen,' a sense still preserved in words like 皇后 (empress). Since simplification, 后 also stands in for the historically separate character 後 ('behind, after'), which pictured a foot trailing along on a path.
夂 (to go) — heading out.
田 (farm field) — going out to the fields ahead of the harvest season, the act of preparation giving 备 its meaning 'to prepare, get ready.'

example.hanzi: 公司为电力中断准备了后备发电机。
example.pinyin: gōngsī wèi diànlì zhōngduàn zhǔnbèi le hòubèi fādiànjī.
example.english: The company prepared a backup generator in case of power outages.
example.fact: The International Space Station maintains multiple redundant backup systems for oxygen, water, and power, including several independent life-support pathways. Because no repair crew can reach the station quickly, engineers design every critical system with at least one backup in case the primary one fails.

components.note: 王 (jade, written without its dot) — 玩 originally meant to handle and admire a piece of jade, extending to 'to play, to have fun.'
元 (yuán) gives a sound distantly related to wán, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — 偶 originally described a wooden figure or idol shaped like a person, later extending to 'a pair' and 'by chance.'
禺 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to 偶's reading ǒu, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 她的房间里摆满了各种玩偶。
example.pinyin: tā de fángjiān lǐ bǎi mǎn le gèzhǒng wánǒu.
example.english: Her room is filled with all kinds of dolls.
example.fact: Since Mattel launched the Barbie doll in 1959, it has sold more than a billion units worldwide and has been given over 200 different careers. The doll's shifting jobs over six decades have often been read as a mirror of changing ideas about women's roles in society.

components.note: 页 (head) — relates to 领's meaning 'neck, collar; to lead,' the head/neck area.
令 (lìng) gives a sound hint — 领 is pronounced lǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
土 (earth) — 域 names a bounded area of land, a territory.
或 (huò) reflects the character's historical phonetic root; the modern reading yù has since diverged.

example.hanzi: 人工智能是当今发展最快的科技领域之一。
example.pinyin: réngōng zhìnéng shì dāngjīn fāzhǎn zuì kuài de kējì lǐngyù zhī yī.
example.english: Artificial intelligence is one of the fastest-developing fields in technology today.
example.fact: The term 'artificial intelligence' was coined in 1956 at the Dartmouth Summer Research Project, a workshop attended by fewer than 20 researchers. They optimistically believed a machine could be built to reason like a human within a single summer, a goal that took many more decades to even partially realize.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.
纟 (thread) — 缘 originally described the hemmed edge of cloth, extended to mean 'connection, fate.'
彖 (tuàn) gives a sound distantly related to yuán, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 那只鹿站在森林的边缘警觉地望着四周。
example.pinyin: nà zhī lù zhàn zài sēnlín de biānyuán jǐngjué de wàng zhe sìzhōu.
example.english: The deer stood at the edge of the forest, watching its surroundings alertly.
example.fact: Ecologists have found that the outer edges of tropical rainforests lose moisture and biodiversity faster than the interior, because sun and wind exposure can dry out soil up to a kilometer inward. This 'edge effect' is a major concern in the Amazon, where deforestation keeps fragmenting the forest into more and more exposed edges.

components.note: 大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).

example.hanzi: 骑自行车时一定要戴头部保护装置。
example.pinyin: qí zìxíngchē shí yīdìng yào dài tóubù bǎohù zhuāngzhì.
example.english: You must wear head protection when riding a bicycle.
example.fact: The human head makes up only about 8 percent of total body weight, but the brain inside it consumes roughly 20 percent of the body's resting energy. No other organ uses anywhere near that share of the body's fuel relative to its size.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates to 清's meaning 'clear (water), pure.'
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 清 is also pronounced qīng, an exact match.

单 is simplified from 單, an ancient pictograph believed to show a forked hunting tool, likely a sling or forked stick used to catch birds and small game. The character was later borrowed to mean 'single, one,' with its original hunting-tool sense fading from common use.

example.hanzi: 出发前她检查了一遍行李清单。
example.pinyin: chūfā qián tā jiǎnchá le yī biàn xínglǐ qīngdān.
example.english: Before departure, she went through her packing checklist once.
example.fact: Surgeon Atul Gawande helped popularize the surgical safety checklist after a 2009 WHO-backed study across eight hospitals worldwide. Simply requiring teams to confirm a short list of basic steps before operating cut major surgical complications by more than a third.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 振 describes shaking or waving something with the hand.
辰 (chén) gives a sound distantly related to zhèn, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 经历失败后，他很快振作起来重新开始训练。
example.pinyin: jīnglì shībài hòu, tā hěn kuài zhènzuò qǐlái chóngxīn kāishǐ xùnliàn.
example.english: After the failure, he quickly pulled himself together and resumed training.
example.fact: Michael Jordan was cut from his high school varsity basketball team as a sophomore. He later said the setback fueled the relentless training habits that helped him become one of the greatest players in NBA history.

components.note: 充 is built on 儿 (a person) at its base, with the upper strokes tracing a child growing tall. This image of steady growth gave 充 its meaning 'to fill, to be full, sufficient.'
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'

example.hanzi: 做这个决定之前，我们需要充分的证据。
example.pinyin: zuò zhège juédìng zhīqián, wǒmen xūyào chōngfèn de zhèngjù.
example.english: Before making this decision, we need sufficient evidence.
example.fact: The Royal Society's Philosophical Transactions, launched in 1665, is considered the first scientific journal to systematically require sufficient supporting evidence before publishing a claim. That review process eventually grew into the peer-review system scientific journals still use today.

meanings: (lit. and fig.) to come back to life

components.note: 亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'
氵 (water) — 活 relates to water flowing, a symbol of life and vitality.
舌 (shé) gives a hint of the sound — 活 is pronounced huó, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 科学家试图利用基因技术复活已灭绝的物种。
example.pinyin: kēxuéjiā shìtú lìyòng jīyīn jìshù fùhuó yǐ mièjué de wùzhǒng.
example.english: Scientists are trying to use genetic technology to revive extinct species.
example.fact: In 2023, researchers successfully extracted RNA from a 130-year-old preserved Tasmanian tiger specimen, the first time RNA had ever been recovered from an extinct species. Some scientists hope such molecules could eventually support 'de-extinction' efforts, though a living Tasmanian tiger remains far off.

components.note: 又 (hand), doubled — two hands side by side depict a pair, giving 双 its meaning 'pair, both, two.'
⺼ (flesh/body) — 胞 relates to the body, originally the womb.
包 (bāo) is an exact match for the sound of 胞.
⺼ (flesh) — 胎 originally named an unborn child inside the body.
台 (tái) gives the sound — a close match for tāi, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这对双胞胎从小就形影不离。
example.pinyin: zhè duì shuāngbāotāi cóngxiǎo jiù xíngyǐngbùlí.
example.english: These twins have been inseparable since childhood.
example.fact: Identical twins form when a single fertilized egg splits into two embryos, giving them nearly identical DNA. Even so, their fingerprints still differ, because ridge patterns are shaped partly by random pressure and position inside the womb rather than genetics alone.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
阝 (a mound/formation) — soldiers arranged in position
车 (chariot) — war chariots lined up in formation
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他们在公园里聊了一阵子才离开。
example.pinyin: tāmen zài gōngyuán lǐ liáo le yī zhènzi cái líkāi.
example.english: They chatted in the park for a while before leaving.
example.fact: A 'jiffy' is an informal but sometimes formally used unit of time, defined in physics as roughly 33.4 picoseconds — the time light takes to travel one centimeter — while in early computing it instead meant about 1/100th of a second, depending on the field using it.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — used when asking a question aloud
那 (nà) gives a sound close to 哪's reading nǎ, differing mainly in tone
二 (two) — 些 originally suggested a small plural amount, building on the idea of 'more than one.'
此 (cǐ) is the historical phonetic element; it no longer closely matches the modern reading xiē.

example.hanzi: 你知道哪些国家使用人民币作为官方货币吗？
example.pinyin: nǐ zhīdào nǎxiē guójiā shǐyòng rénmínbì zuòwéi guānfāng huòbì ma?
example.english: Do you know which countries use the renminbi as their official currency?
example.fact: The US dollar is the official or de facto currency in more than a dozen countries outside the United States, including Ecuador, El Salvador, and Zimbabwe. Each of these countries 'dollarized' its economy after a period of severe hyperinflation made its own currency unusable.

components.note: 彡 (hair/decorative strokes) — 修 relates to grooming, decorating, or improving something
攸 (yōu) gives a sound close to 修's reading xiū, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 师傅正在修理那台坏掉的洗衣机。
example.pinyin: shīfu zhèngzài xiūlǐ nà tái huàidiào de xǐyījī.
example.english: The technician is repairing that broken washing machine.
example.fact: Shortly after the Hubble Space Telescope launched in 1990, engineers discovered a flaw in its main mirror that blurred its images. A 1993 space shuttle repair mission installed corrective optics, fixing Hubble's vision and enabling it to later capture famous images like the 'Pillars of Creation.'

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — resemblance here is tied to physical, bodily likeness.
⺌ (a form related to 小, 'small') gives the sound — a close match for xiào, differing only in tone.
心 (heart) — 恩 relates to feelings of gratitude and kindness.
因 (yīn) gives the sound — an exact match with 恩.

example.hanzi: 肖恩每天早上都去公园跑步。
example.pinyin: Xiāo ēn měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
example.english: Sean goes jogging in the park every morning.
example.fact: The name 'Sean' is the Anglicized spelling of the Irish 'Seán,' which itself descends from the Hebrew name 'John' by way of the French 'Jean.' The chain reflects centuries of contact between Irish, French, and Biblical naming traditions.

components.note: 爻 (crossed strands) pictures threads woven in a loose, open pattern, the kind of sparse weave that stood out as unusual.
巾 (cloth) grounds the image in actual fabric; a loosely woven, uncommon cloth gave 希 its meaning 'rare, scarce,' later extended to 'to hope for' something not easily had.
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.
力 (strength) — 勒 relates to tightening or restraining with force.
革 (gé) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading lēi has diverged considerably.

example.hanzi: 历史课上老师讲述了希特勒发动战争的历史背景。
example.pinyin: lìshǐ kè shàng lǎoshī jiǎngshù le Xītèlè fādòng zhànzhēng de lìshǐ bèijǐng.
example.english: In history class, the teacher explained the historical background of Hitler starting the war.
example.fact: Adolf Hitler applied to Vienna's Academy of Fine Arts twice as a young man and was rejected both times before turning to politics. Historians still cite this documented failure when speculating about how differently the 20th century might have unfolded.

components.note: 夭 (a person leaning back) — the pose of someone laughing.
⺮ (bamboo-like strokes) — suggesting a wide grin, giving 笑 its meaning 'to laugh, smile.'
宀 (roof/house) — 容's meaning 'to contain, hold' relates to a house holding things, extended to 'appearance, to allow, tolerate.'

example.hanzi: 她脸上一直挂着温暖的笑容。
example.pinyin: tā liǎn shàng yīzhí guà zhe wēnnuǎn de xiàoróng.
example.english: She always had a warm smile on her face.
example.fact: Genuine smiles, known to researchers as Duchenne smiles, engage both the mouth muscles and the orbicularis oculi muscles around the eyes. Studies show people can usually tell a genuine smile from a posed one within a fraction of a second, even from a photograph.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — relates to 据's meaning 'to rely on, according to,' as if grasping evidence in hand.
居 (jū) gave the base sound; the pronunciation later shifted to jù, keeping the same final but a different tone.
讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō

example.hanzi: 据说这座古庙已经有上千年的历史了。
example.pinyin: jùshuō zhè zuò gǔmiào yǐjīng yǒu shàng qiān nián de lìshǐ le.
example.english: It is said that this ancient temple has a history of over a thousand years.
example.fact: Angkor Wat in Cambodia, often called the largest religious monument in the world, was originally built as a Hindu temple in the early 12th century. Over the following centuries it gradually transformed into a Buddhist site, a shift still visible in its carvings today.

components.note: 电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'
氵 (water) shows 池 relates to a body of water.
也 (yě) gives a sound distantly related to chí, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 手机的电池只剩下百分之十的电量。
example.pinyin: shǒujī de diànchí zhǐ shèng xià bǎi fēn zhī shí de diànliàng.
example.english: The phone's battery only has 10 percent power left.
example.fact: Sony commercialized the first lithium-ion battery in 1991, and the technology now powers nearly every smartphone and electric vehicle. Its inventors, John Goodenough, M. Stanley Whittingham, and Akira Yoshino, shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing it.

components.note: 户 (door) — 居 relates to where one lives, behind a door
古 (gǔ) gives a sound related to 居's reading jū, from an older, closer pronunciation link
巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.

example.hanzi: 当地居民对新建的工厂表示强烈反对。
example.pinyin: dāngdì jūmín duì xīnjiàn de gōngchǎng biǎoshì qiángliè fǎnduì.
example.english: Local residents strongly opposed the newly built factory.
example.fact: Greater Tokyo is home to roughly 37 million residents, making it the most populous urban area on Earth. That single metropolitan area holds more people than the entire population of Canada.

components.note: 平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'

example.hanzi: 家人只希望他能平安回家。
example.pinyin: jiārén zhǐ xīwàng tā néng píng'ān huí jiā.
example.english: His family only hoped he could return home safe and sound.
example.fact: The 'black box' flight recorders carried on commercial aircraft are actually painted bright orange, not black. The color is chosen specifically so rescue teams can spot the device quickly among wreckage after a crash.

components.note: Hand — moving things is done by hand.
Gives the sound bān, matching the character's reading.
土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.

example.hanzi: 他们上个月把所有家具都搬走了。
example.pinyin: tāmen shàng gè yuè bǎ suǒyǒu jiājù dōu bān zǒu le.
example.english: They moved all the furniture away last month.
example.fact: In 1999, engineers moved the entire 4,800-ton Cape Hatteras Lighthouse nearly 2,900 feet inland on steel rails and rollers to save it from coastal erosion. It remains one of the largest brick structure relocations ever carried out.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — an older semantic link to beeswax, made by insects.
昔 (xī) gives a sound distantly related to là, having drifted apart over time.
火 (fire) — 烛 relates to a flame.
虫 (chóng) gives a sound distantly related to zhú, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 生日蛋糕上插满了蜡烛。
example.pinyin: shēngrì dàngāo shàng chā mǎn le làzhú.
example.english: The birthday cake was covered with candles.
example.fact: Before electric lighting, candles were commonly made from tallow (animal fat) or beeswax. Beeswax candles burned much cleaner and longer than tallow ones, which made them a costly luxury reserved mostly for churches and wealthy households in medieval Europe.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.

六 was originally a pictograph of a simple hut or shelter, with its roof and supporting beams still visible in the shape. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the number 'six,' a use unrelated to its original architectural meaning.

example.hanzi: 我们星期六约好一起去爬山。
example.pinyin: wǒmen Xīngqīliù yuē hǎo yīqǐ qù páshān.
example.english: We agreed to go hiking together on Saturday.
example.fact: Saturday is the only day of the week in English named directly after a Roman deity, Saturn, while most other English weekday names come from Norse gods instead. The mismatch is a linguistic leftover from Roman astrology blending with later Germanic naming traditions.

components.note: 木 (tree) — traditionally read as a tree that has borne fruit.
立 (standing) — standing close by to watch it grow, evoking closeness and nurture, extended to 亲's meaning 'close, dear; parent, relative.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 生病的时候，最想见到的就是亲人。
example.pinyin: shēngbìng de shíhòu, zuì xiǎng jiàndào de jiùshì qīnrén.
example.english: When you're sick, the people you most want to see are your close relatives.
example.fact: Researchers studying elephant social bonds have found that they maintain lifelong relationships with close relatives. Grieving elephants have even been observed returning repeatedly to the bones of deceased family members, touching and investigating the remains for years afterward.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.

乡 is simplified from 鄉, an ancient pictograph showing two kneeling figures facing a shared food vessel between them, the image of people gathered for a communal meal in a settlement. This gave 乡 its meaning 'village, countryside, hometown.'

example.hanzi: 每年春节，他都会回家乡看望父母。
example.pinyin: měinián chūnjié, tā dōu huì huí jiāxiāng kànwàng fùmǔ.
example.english: Every Spring Festival, he returns to his hometown to visit his parents.
example.fact: China's Spring Festival travel rush, known as chunyun, is the largest annual human migration on Earth, with billions of trips made in about 40 days. Most of that movement is people returning to their hometowns for the holiday before heading back to work afterward.

components.note: 丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
上 (top) — the upper edge pressing down
卜 — the lower edge, with a card squeezed between the two
囗 (an enclosure) frames the character, picturing a bounded space such as a mat or room.
大 (a person, arms and legs outstretched) shown resting inside the enclosure above gave 因 its meaning 'to rely on, cause, because of.'

example.hanzi: 警方在仓库里查获了大量可卡因。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng zài cāngkù lǐ cháhuò le dàliàng kěkǎyīn.
example.english: Police seized a large quantity of cocaine in the warehouse.
example.fact: Cocaine comes from the leaves of the coca plant native to the Andes, which indigenous peoples there have chewed for thousands of years to fight altitude sickness and fatigue at high elevation. The active alkaloid itself was not chemically isolated until 1860.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迅 relates to fast movement.
卂 pictures something darting forward quickly, giving 迅 its meaning 'rapid, fast.'
辶 (to walk/move) — 速 relates to the speed of movement
束 (shù) gives a loose sound connection to 速's reading sù

example.hanzi: 消防员迅速赶到现场展开救援。
example.pinyin: xiāofángyuán xùnsù gǎndào xiànchǎng zhǎnkāi jiùyuán.
example.english: The firefighters rapidly arrived at the scene to begin the rescue.
example.fact: Peregrine falcons can exceed 320 kilometers per hour during a hunting dive, making them the fastest animals on Earth by a wide margin. Specialized bony structures in their nostrils let them keep breathing safely despite the extreme airflow at that speed.

components.note: 米 (grain, especially husked rice) — 精's meaning 'refined, essence, spirit' relates to rice refined to its purest form.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 精 is pronounced jīng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.
疒 (sickness) — relates directly to 病's meaning 'illness, disease, to be sick.'
丙 (bǐng) gives a sound hint — 病 is pronounced bìng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这项研究揭示了压力与精神病之间的关系。
example.pinyin: zhè xiàng yánjiū jiēshì le yālì yǔ jīngshénbìng zhījiān de guānxì.
example.english: This study reveals the relationship between stress and mental illness.
example.fact: The World Health Organization estimates that roughly one in eight people worldwide lives with a mental disorder, and depression alone is among the leading causes of disability globally. Yet mental health typically receives less than 2 percent of average government health budgets.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 棺 names a wooden box used for burial, a coffin.
官 (guān) gives the sound — an exact match with 棺.
木 (wood) — 材 originally named timber.
才 (cái) gives the sound — an exact match with 材.

example.hanzi: 工人们小心地把棺材抬进墓地。
example.pinyin: gōngrénmen xiǎoxīn de bǎ guāncai tái jìn mùdì.
example.english: The workers carefully carried the coffin into the cemetery.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptian pharaohs were often buried in nested sets of coffins, sometimes three or more, one placed inside another. Tutankhamun's innermost coffin was made of solid gold and weighed about 110 kilograms.

components.note: 页 (head) — relates to 领's meaning 'neck, collar; to lead,' the head/neck area.
令 (lìng) gives a sound hint — 领 is pronounced lǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'

example.hanzi: 他每天上班都会打一条整齐的领带。
example.pinyin: tā měitiān shàngbān dōu huì dǎ yī tiáo zhěngqí de lǐngdài.
example.english: He wears a neatly tied necktie to work every day.
example.fact: The modern necktie is often traced to Croatian mercenaries serving in the French army in the 1660s, whose knotted neck scarves caught the eye of French nobility. Over the following centuries that accessory evolved through several styles into the necktie worn today.

components.note: The character traces the front view of an ox's head, with the top stroke and crossing lines representing its curved horns and ears.
扌 (hand) — 排 relates to arranging things by hand into order
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to 排's reading pái, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的牛排非常鲜嫩多汁。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā cāntīng de niúpái fēicháng xiānnèn duōzhī.
example.english: The steak at this restaurant is very tender and juicy.
example.fact: Wagyu cattle, prized for their intensely marbled beef, are raised in Japan under strict genetic lineage tracking. Each animal's pedigree can be traced back through registered records much like a racehorse's, which helps preserve the breed's distinctive marbling.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
开 (open, here representing a frame or opening) — 形 pictures light passing through a gap.
彡 (streaks or rays of light) — light and pattern coming through an opening gave 形 its meaning 'shape' or 'form.'

example.hanzi: 医生详细说明了病人目前的情形。
example.pinyin: yīshēng xiángxì shuōmíng le bìngrén mùqián de qíngxing.
example.english: The doctor explained the patient's current situation in detail.
example.fact: Triage, the practice of assessing patients to decide who is treated first, originated on Napoleonic battlefields in the early 1800s. French military surgeon Dominique Jean Larrey developed the system to make sure the most urgent casualties were treated before less severe ones.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — work involving livestock, done imperfectly
工 (work) — the labor itself, linked to the idea of falling short
力 (strength) — 劲 names physical strength or energy.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的特效真是差劲。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng de tèxiào zhēnshi chàjìn.
example.english: The special effects in this movie are really disappointing.
example.fact: The 1980 film 'Heaven's Gate' was such a critically panned, costly box-office failure that it lost the equivalent of roughly 100 million of today's dollars. Its collapse is often cited by film historians as a major cause of the fall of United Artists studio.

components.note: 前's upper element traces back to 止, a foot shown pointing ahead, while its lower element was originally 舟, a boat. The image of a foot moving forward aboard a boat gave 前 its meaning 'front, forward, before.'
辶 (to walk) — 途 names a road or path traveled on.
余 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tú, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 老师说他很有前途，应该继续深造。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī shuō tā hěn yǒu qiántú, yīnggāi jìxù shēnzào.
example.english: The teacher said he has great prospects and should continue his studies.
example.fact: Albert Einstein struggled to find an academic position after graduating and worked for several years as a patent clerk in Switzerland. That unpromising start came before he published his theory of special relativity in 1905, at the age of 26.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 他把书包放在椅子边上。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ shūbāo fàng zài yǐzi biānshàng.
example.english: He put his backpack beside the chair.
example.fact: Earth's magnetic north pole is not fixed at one spot but drifts constantly, having moved over 600 kilometers since 1900. It is currently migrating from northern Canada toward Siberia at roughly 50 kilometers per year, driven by changes deep in Earth's molten outer core.
